classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the buildings' height difference as a shorter side of a right-angled triangle.

content.prompt:
Calculate the difference in height between these two buildings.
Round your answer to 1 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 building diagram beneath the prompt
spec.description: Shorter building on the left and taller building on the right, with windows and doors, a shared ground line, a top-to-top sloping segment and a horizontal separation arrow.
spec.mathematics: The sloping segment joins the facing upper corners and is 62.3 m long. The facing building edges are 25 m apart horizontally. Their height difference is the unknown vertical leg.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the height difference and solution construction are absent.

answer.worked:
The height difference $d$ is the vertical shorter side.
$$\begin{align*}d &= \sqrt{62.3^2-25^2}\\d &= \sqrt{3256.29}\\d &\approx 57.1\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$
